findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical endpoint-and-difference dynamic program. endings, difference, and extensions expose the state and transition directly, the pair contribution is expressed without incidental machinery, and an inert candidate would not materially improve this expert interview solution.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 446 and its Python integer-array-to-count surface. The app solve signature and native numberOfArithmeticSlices method use the same input and integer result. The modular Reference preserves the subsequence and arithmetic definitions, minimum length, signed value domain, and signed-32-bit result guarantee.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064836354. The app and native implementations allocate the same endpoint maps, visit the same left-right index pairs, compute the same differences and extension counts, add only length-at-least-three extensions to the answer, and retain each new pair plus its extensions; only annotations and the Solution wrapper differ.

The benchmark was repaired because the former equal-value tiers violated the source guarantee that the answer fits a signed 32-bit integer. The new 128-, 256-, and 512-element tiers span 4x and use distinct bit-reversal-ordered numbers whose ternary digits are only zero or one, proving that no three values form an arithmetic progression and the legal expected count is zero. The protected O(n^2) source passed all 10 opaque correctness executions and all three ordinary performance tiers at 1.02x. With only the internal line-event safety allowance raised so it could terminate, a correct repeated-prefix-sort control passed every output but failed only the growth verdict at 4.13x.

The Approach exactly defines each endpoint-and-difference state, explains why two-element pairs are stored but not counted, derives the extension transition and unique counting argument, and states the correct O(n^2) time and space bounds. Its alternatives now also identify repeated prefix sorting as the superquadratic control represented by the benchmark.

The hash-bound Reference was checked against the live public statement. It preserves the arithmetic-sequence examples and non-example, subsequence definition and selection example, 32-bit result guarantee, both exact source examples and their complete explanations, and both constraints. The fabricated third example in the legacy document was removed because the live source has exactly two examples.
